subject: Capacity blueprint: private GPU pool simulation results & rollout constraints
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Priyanka Rao <priyanka@cobaltcloud.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity blueprint: private GPU pool simulation results & rollout constraints

Hi Priyanka —

Thanks for agreeing to the simulation window next week. Attached is the configuration we plan to run on your VPC-scale test cluster (see sim_config snippet attached). High-level asks:

- Run three steady-state scenarios (50%, 75%, 100% target util for 1, 4, 12-hour windows).
- One spike test: 3x burst for 10 minutes to observe autoscaler reaction and tail-latency behavior.
- Network isolation/egress: confirm whether egress throttling is applied on your side. We need line-rate tests for large prompt loads.

We expect to measure sustained throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU and the 95/99th token latencies. The goals for CobaltCloud (per initial SOW):
- Target throughput: 120k tokens/sec cluster-wide at p95 < 250ms for short-form prompts (avg 64 tokens).
- Graceful degradation: if per-shard latency exceeds 350ms, fallback to reduced concurrency mode and route to Redwood-hosted fallback.

Please confirm infra-team availability and attach any constraints (NIC, MTU, RDMA, kernel versions). I attached sim_results_q1_runA.csv (previous baseline) and the capacity_model_v2.xlsx for your reference.

Thanks —
Tessa
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sim_config.yaml (text), capacity_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Priyanka Rao <priyanka@cobaltcloud.com>

Cc: infra-team@cobaltcloud.com
Date: 2027-01-13T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity blueprint: private GPU pool simulation results & rollout constraints

Tessa —

Thanks for the plan. Infra team confirms availability for 2027-01-18 to 01-19 slot. A few constraints from our side:

- NICs: 100GbE with 2x dual-port, but not using RoCEv2 in prod test, so no RDMA for the baseline run.
- MTU: 1500 by default; enabling jumbo frames requires change control + 24h notice.
- Kernel: RHEL 8.6 with tuned profile; we can enable CPU isolation and hugepages.
- Disk: local NVMe on worker nodes; we will not use shared NFS mounts for KV cache persistence.

We'll attach our initial run (sim_results_q1_runA.csv) from a smaller cluster for context. For the spike test, infra will throttle egress at 8Gbps peak unless you request an exception.

Questions:
1) Is the fallback to Redwood-hosted inference acceptable if we hit degraded latency? We need operational playbook for data path changes.
2) Can you provide the client-side concurrency settings to use during test (tokens-per-request, concurrency per client)?

- Priyanka
Head of Platform, CobaltCloud

Attachments: sim_results_q1_runA.csv (csv)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyanka Rao <priyanka@cobaltcloud.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity blueprint: private GPU pool simulation results & rollout constraints

Priyanka / team —

Couple of technical notes to align expectations on measurement and autoscaling:

- NUMA / GPU affinity: if your nodes have 2 sockets and 8 GPUs, pinning processes to a single NUMA zone improved p95 by ~12% in our internal runs. We'll provide a pinned container image.
- No RDMA: without RoCE, inter-GPU KV cache sharing will add ~8-15ms p95 depending on sequence length; expect slightly lower throughput per GPU vs our RDMA baseline.
- Batching strategy: use dynamic batching with a 20ms hold window for steady-state scenarios. For spike runs set hold window to 5ms to avoid queue build-up.
- Autoscaler thresholds: recommend scale-up at 70% GPU utilization sustained for 90s, scale-down at <45% sustained for 3m. Add a cooldown of 2m to avoid thrash.
- Graceful degradation: we will implement a 'reduced-concurrency' profile that reduces max concurrency by 40% and switches model variant to a quantized 4-bit variant to preserve latency while sacrificing some quality.

I'll attach a short README with runtime knobs. Also: measure token emit rate and per-request prompt length distribution — synthetic tests often overestimate throughput because they use constant short prompts.

- Dev
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runtime_notes.md (txt)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyanka Rao <priyanka@cobaltcloud.com>
Date: 2027-01-15T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity blueprint: private GPU pool simulation results & rollout constraints

Team —

I pulled capacity_model_v2.xlsx and ran a couple of what-if scenarios tied to the SOW. Quick takeaways for the commercial side:

- If target sustained throughput is 120k tokens/sec (p95 <250ms), estimated reservation is 42 x A300-equivalent GPUs with standard (no RDMA) networking — this assumes 64-token avg and our dynamic batching.
- With RDMA / jumbo frames enabled we see ~15% GPU reduction (approx 36 GPUs).
- Burst SLA (3x for 10 minutes): recommend a short-term burst pool of 8 GPUs (reserved) plus transient cloud fallback up to 10k tokens/sec to cover peaks.

Risks & mitigations:
- Network MTU change control could delay RDMA enablement — propose running baseline tests now, and a separate RDMA-optimized run after change control completes.
- Autoscaler settings above look good; consider adding circuit-breaker that prevents scale-down when error rate > 1%.

I've filed INFRA-8721 to track follow-ups and scheduling. I'll also share a Drive link with the spreadsheet and a price delta table.

- Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx), price_delta_table.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Capacity blueprint: private GPU pool simulation results & rollout constraints

Thanks everyone — short summary & next steps (action owners in parentheses):

1) Test window confirmed: 2027-01-18 09:00 - 18:00 PST (Cobalt infra). (Priyanka)
2) Baseline targets:
   - Sustained throughput goal: 120k tokens/sec cluster-wide at p95 <250ms (Tessa/Marissa)
   - Fallback: reduced-concurrency + quantized model variant; route overflow to Redwood-hosted for critical requests (Dev)
3) Autoscaler: scale-up at 70% sustained for 90s; scale-down <45% for 3m; cooldown 2m; circuit-breaker if error rate >1% (Dev)
4) Network constraints: no RDMA / MTU 1500 for baseline — run RDMA-optimized pass after change control (Priyanka)
5) Capacity estimate: reserve 42 A300-equivalent GPUs baseline; optional RDMA optimization reduces to ~36 (Marissa)
6) Deliverables before run: pinned container image + runtime_notes.md (Dev), final sim config (Tessa), access keys and run window confirmation (Priyanka)

I'll own post-run synthesis and the decision on reserved capacity vs Dedicated commit. Naomi - please prepare a short cost/ops risk slide for the 1/20 leadership sync.

Best —
Tessa
